chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died and left behind his wife, his sister, and his grandfather. He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is from four shares: for the wife is the quarter, and for the sister is one share, and for the grandfather are two shares.'
ai.seo_question: How is an estate divided when a deceased leaves behind a wife, a sister, and a grandfather?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific shares for a wife, sister, and paternal grandfather, establishing a four-share division where the grandfather receives two shares alongside the sister. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential approach to resolving potential conflicts between the grandfather and other heirs, emphasizing the grandfather's significant portion in the absence of closer male ascendants like a father. This ruling underscores the practical application of inheritance laws in early Shia scholarship, particularly in the context of al-Kulayni's compilation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who died and left his wife, and his sister, and his grandfather. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is from four shares – for the wife is the quarter, and for the sister is one share (a quarter), and for the grandfather are two shares (half)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from abu ‘Ubaydah who has narrated the following:

“About the case of a man who dies and leaves behind his wife, sister and grandfather, abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘This is distributed from four parts, one-fourth for the woman, one share for the sister and two shares for the grandfather.’”
